A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same global and neuron-level persistent-homology study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support matching retained content despite the changed title and extensive redesign.

before.justification: V1 reports original analyses of LLM activations, PH-based classification results, neuron-permutation controls, dispersion analyses, and computational measurements in Section 4 and Appendices A–C.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports linear-classifier comparisons and an adaptive prompt-injection experiment in Table 1 and Appendix C.5.

M1.justification: The proposed procedures remain Vietoris–Rips PH, 41-dimensional barcode summaries, correlation pruning, PCA/CCA, logistic regression with SHAP, and paired-layer 2D neuron embeddings. The newly evaluated sparse autoencoders are comparison methods; the PH method itself is unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds LLMail-Inject examples designed to evade defenses, extending evaluation to an adaptive XPIA scenario. This is a focused addition on Mistral at one layer. TaskTracker and WMDP-inspired sandbagging coverage remain; newly named TaskTracker source benchmarks do not establish additional evaluations.

E2.justification: V1 contains no corresponding comparison against conventional activation classifiers. V2 Table 1 introduces LDA, linear SVM, and logistic regression, each evaluated on raw activations and sparse-autoencoder representations. This adds a substantive comparative component rather than merely extending existing comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols classify 1,000 clean and 1,000 poisoned individual activations with a 70/30 split and optional 128-dimensional SAE representations, and evaluate adaptive attacks using 100 generated clean counterparts at Mistral layer 16. Appendix B.1 also changes the stated PH subsample size from 1,000 to 4,096, already specified elsewhere in v1. This is a reported setting revision; a rerun is not established.

E4.justification: Appendix C.5 adds a focused robustness test asking whether PH signatures persist for attacks designed to evade activation-based defenses. Existing normalization and permutation controls, within-class and mixed-data ablations, layer-gap analyses, and variance-peak analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 revises the reported repeated-subsampling budget from 300 PH subsamples per condition to 64 per condition, bringing it closer to the retained main-text and C.4 descriptions. This changes documented Monte Carlo sampling information without establishing additional runs. Existing cross-validation, permutation tests, Welch/FDR tests, bootstrap counts, and uncertainty reports remain.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantive comparative findings: Table 1 reports raw LDA accuracy of 0.9950 at layer 0 and 1.0000 at later listed layers. Table 8 adds adaptive-attack results, including 12 versus 4 loops and median H1 birth times of 69.36 versus 84.92 for clean versus attack activations. Figure 17 adds loop-count distributions. Earlier classifier scores and summary tables are retained; these additions do not establish same-setting PH performance gains.

T1.justification: Persistent-entropy and dispersion-ratio formulas, activation definitions, and the underlying PH construction remain unchanged. V2 expands the explanation of Vietoris–Rips complexes and barcode vectorization but adds no substantive theorem, proof, derivation, or revised mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The topological-compression and neuron-level PH contributions remain. V2 explicitly acknowledges in the introduction that standard linear classifiers also separate normal and adversarial activations, and presents PH as explaining that separability geometrically. This qualifies v1's headline emphasis on near-perfect PH separation.

C2.justification: Section 5 develops new substantive arguments about relational geometry versus SAE features, cross-model comparability, and linear probes approximating underlying topological structure. Appendix C.5 additionally interprets the opposing mean and median H0-death trends through low-scale merging components. The memory and subsampling limitations are substantially retained.

D1.justification: V2 documents the SAE dimension and the adaptive experiment's generation and evaluation checkpoints, synthetic-clean construction, and manual verification. Existing hardware, PH software, runtime measurements, and sandbagging collection procedures remain. Appendix C.3 introduces confusing references to both states as 'elicited', although the equations still distinguish locked and elicited activations.

R1.justification: V2 removes v1's dedicated related-work discussion and citations covering PH for language representations and adversarial/OOD detection, including Chauhan and Kaul, Gardinazzi et al., Gebhart and Schrater, and Pollano et al. It adds PH foundations, geometry-related positioning, and benchmark references. This substantially changes research context rather than merely changing citation style.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, PH background, results narrative, and discussion are extensively rewritten. Barcode summaries receive a separate background subsection, the method section becomes 'Experimental Design', and the dedicated related-work subsection disappears. Much appendix prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: Global-analysis plots are extensively redrawn with revised colors, markers, typography, and axes, and Figure 2 is redesigned. Mistral SHAP moves from main-text Figure 9 to appendix Figure 16. Figure 17 changes from two histogram rows to three smoothed-distribution rows, and new Tables 1 and 8 accompany a substantial layout revision.

improvement.justification: V2 offers clearer PH explanations and adds useful baseline and adaptive-attack evidence. However, its claimed baseline advantage compares individual activations with PH summaries of groups, while adaptive validation covers one model/layer with synthetic controls. Removing closely related PH literature and introducing locked/elicited labeling errors also weaken the revision. These material gains and harms leave the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
